subject: Pivotal Health — sudden 5xx spike and request timeouts (impacting inference)
messages:
From: Diego Morales <diego.morales@pivotalhealth.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strange inference failures and spikes in 500s — urgent

Hi Logan,

We started seeing a sudden burst of 500s and request timeouts from Redwood for two of our critical endpoints (patient-summary and triage-scorer) around 08:50 PST. The client-side errors look like: 
- 500 internal_server_error with body: "runtime: concurrent kernel fault" (multiple request-ids attached below)
- Intermittent 504 gateway_timeout for the streaming endpoints

Sample request ids: r-2f7a4d, r-2f7a5c, r-2f7b01. Latency for successful requests also jumped from ~120ms to 2s+ for a while. This is impacting our triage queue and is causing clinical workflows to time out.

I attached a short log snippet and can share full client traces if helpful. Can you confirm this is on your side and provide ETA for mitigation? We have customers experiencing delays and are getting escalations.

Thanks,
Diego
Platform Lead, Pivotal Health
platform@pivotalhealth.com

Attachments: pivotal-500-samples-0707.log (log snippet)

From: logan.wright@redwood.ai
To: Diego Morales <diego.morales@pivotalhealth.com>
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange inference failures and spikes in 500s — urgent

Diego — thanks for the signal and the sample IDs. We're escalating this to an ops bridge now.

What we're doing immediately:
- Spinning up a mitigation bridge and prioritizing your request IDs for trace collection.
- Failing requests will be routed to a compatible model variant to keep throughput for critical endpoints.
- Collecting runtime traces and GPU telemetry (ben is taking lead on that).

Info we need from you (if available):
- A short window with full client-side timestamps (start/end) for a couple of the failing calls.
- Any recent changes to request size or batching config on your side.

I'll circulate a customer-facing update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as a SEV-1.

— Logan
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
To: Diego Morales <diego.morales@pivotalhealth.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2026 09:49:00 -07:00
Subject: Pivotal Health — initial incident update (we have a mitigation)

Diego — quick customer-facing update from the bridge: 

Summary (what we saw):
- Around 08:50 PST several Redwood runtime nodes serving the patient-summary and triage-scorer routes experienced elevated kernel-level faults coincident with a spike in concurrent request queue length. This resulted in increased 5xx responses and timeouts for ~18 minutes.

Impact:
- Approx 12% of requests across the two routes returned 5xx or timed out during the spike window. Some customers saw elevated latencies between 08:50–09:08 PST.

What we did (mitigation):
- Automatically routed traffic away from affected nodes and activated a compatible, smaller-model fallback for streaming to keep connections alive.
- Transient failures were retried with jitter; we applied conservative rate-dampening for high-concurrency clients.
- We captured GPU and runtime traces and pulled a targeted log bundle (attached).

Current status:
- The majority of traffic has stabilized and error rates are back to baseline as of 09:07 PST. We are continuing to monitor and collect traces for root cause analysis.

Next steps & ETA: 
- Ben will dig into kernel/GPU trace correlation and share preliminary findings by 15:00 PST today.
- We will follow up with a short exec-facing update and a postmortem draft within 24 hours.

Attachments: redwood-runtime-traces-0707.zip (trace bundle)

We understand the operational impact and will prioritize the RCA and any remediation work. Please ping me directly if you need a faster channel (phone or DM).

— Evelyn Hart
Director, Incident Response & Reliability Communications
Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: Diego Morales <diego.morales@pivotalhealth.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Pivotal Health — post-incident follow-up and action items

Diego — quick follow-up with findings and actions from our postmortem draft. Thanks again for the traces; those were helpful.

Root cause (summary):
- An intermittent kernel-level timeout in the NVidia driver on a subset of older GPU hosts coincided with a traffic-pattern shift that increased concurrent KV cache memory churn. The combined conditions led to transient runtime faults on 3/48 nodes serving your routes.

Actions we're taking (short- and medium-term):
- Immediate: remove affected hosts from the serving pool and replace with validated nodes (completed 07/07 10:00 PST).
- 24h: apply a runtime patch to improve kernel fault detection and safer thread-level backoff (targeted rollout 07/09).
- 30d: expand pre-live stress tests to include KV churn patterns observed in your workload and add guardrails in our scheduling policy.

Customer-facing commitments:
- We'll share a final postmortem doc and timeline within 72 hours (link below).
- We'll create a targeted alert for any similar kernel/kv-churn signature and offer a joint runbook session to tune retries and batching.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-pivotal-0708.pdf (draft)
Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/pivotal-postmortem-0708, https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-1249

If you'd like a short readout with your platform team, we can schedule 30 minutes tomorrow.

— Ben Carter
Sr. Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
